_note: Numbers from 'Carryover: Definitions and Fading Rules'. The team confirms them in the call. If a number changes, change it here only. Per-task times (start_time_seconds, long_pause_seconds) live in each task file; a step's own long_pause_seconds overrides the task's.

help_levels._note: Most help = step + small steps (mode 'split'). Some help = short name (mode 'hint'). No help = folded under 'See all steps' (mode 'hide').

check_questions._note: Only for folded (no help) steps that have a check_question. Asked at the end of the task.

terms.small_steps: The hidden steps inside a step. Shown one at a time, only if the person wants them.
terms.folded_step: A whole step the person already does on their own, so it is not shown up front. Always one tap away under 'See all steps'.
terms.help: Anything shown beyond the step's short name: the full step, small steps, a start push, a refresher.
terms.start_push: One tiny first action, shown only if someone has trouble starting.
terms.check_question: One question at the end of a task, only for folded steps that are easy to forget.
terms.done_on_their_own: Finished the step without opening any help, and no help appeared by itself (prompted = no).
terms.used_help: Opened help for the step, said yes to 'Want help with this step?', or asked to repeat it. Record how far they opened.
terms.trouble_starting: Opened the task but did not begin the first step: opened 2+ times without starting, took longer than the task's start time, or opened and closed it.
terms.long_pause: No progress on a step for longer than the long-pause time (the step's own, else the task's). Never on steps with wait: true.
terms.struggled: Trouble starting, a long pause at a step, or answered 'No' / 'Something was hard' to a question.
terms.skipped: Never opened the task that day. Not struggling.
terms.usual_break: How long this person normally goes between doing this task.
terms.rusty: This break is more than 2x their usual break for this task, and at least 14 days. New person with no history: 14 days.
